additional_info.subject: ID0468424-DC/Si-D/AT-[RVP/T9170005103] Charging Issue CRM:03288000012
additional_info.body:
Dear Jakob,
Thank you for contacting eMobility Support.
After carefully checking the logs of the timestamp being given, we find that the network went offline during the charging session.
When the network connection goes offline, the charger can`t provide any requests to the backend of the charger, and this is the reason the backend couldn`t respond to the request to stop the charging session.
The network connection can go offline, because of an unstable network connection with the network provider, or because the router had trouble finding a signal.
Right now i see that the network connection is stable and no errors are showing.
Please provide me with feedback if this answered your question, or if you are still facing issues.
Thank you.
Kind regards,
Priscilla van Wettum

additional_info.subject: AW: ID0468424-DC/Si-D/AT-[RVP/T9170005103] Charging Issue CRM:03288000012
additional_info.body:
Dear Priscilla,
Our backend system is locally connected with the charger (not via the internet). Therefore any problem with the internet connection shouldn't have an influence on sending ocpp messages to our backend. We can see that the connection was stable during the whole time, the charger also sent the regular heartbeat messages.
But for some reason no status notification nor authenticate, start_transaction and so on was communicated to our system.
I hope you can figure out what caused this problem.
Kind regards,
Jakob

additional_info.subject: ID0468424-DC/Si-D/AT-[RVP/T9170005103] Charging Issue CRM:03288000012
additional_info.body:
Dear Jakob,
Thank you for your detailed explanation.
We understand that your backend is locally connected to the charger and not communicating via the public internet. Under normal conditions, this setup should indeed allow OCPP messages to be exchanged independently of external internet availability.
However, for the Sicharge D charger, internal network stability and time synchronization are still critical. Even if the physical connection remains established and heartbeat messages are sent successfully, temporary internal communication interruptions (e.g. network interface resets, firewall filtering, or TCP session instability) can cause the charger to suppress or queue certain OCPP messages such as
StatusNotification
,
Authorize
, or
StartTransaction
.
In such situations, the charger may continue sending heartbeat messages while transaction-related messages are not transmitted or are rejected at the session level. This behavior can occur without the charger explicitly dropping the OCPP connection.
If you can provide charger logs from the relevant period, we will be happy to analyze them in more detail and determine the root cause.
Thank you.
Kind regards,
Priscilla van Wettum
